deep.reconstruction:
Context: May 1832 magnetometer work, the experiments behind 'Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris ad mensuram absolutam revocata' (1832/33). A magnetized needle A lies on a wooden rod carrying a mirror (Holzstab mit Spiegel). Its position along the rod is changed and the oscillation period T is timed at each position. Then the torsion of the suspension is calibrated.

(A) Series 3. The position parameter x is the offset of the south end of the rod from the south end of the needle. Here x = -4.7 mm: the needle projects 4.7 mm beyond the rod on the south side. The provisional period is T' = 30.60 s.

Column 1 gives clock times t_n of the n-th passage, for n = 1..10 and 46..49. Column 2 gives reduced epochs r_n = t_n - n*30.60 s. Each r_n is the time of passage 0 that t_n implies (my verification). For example:
- 1h34m25.4s - 91.8s = 1h32m53.6s.
- 1h38m00.40s - 306.0s = 1h32m54.40s.
- 1h56m18.25s - 1407.6s = 1h32m50.65s.

All entries for n = 2..10 and 46..49 check exactly. This holds provided:
- the minutes of the reduced column are read as 32' (not 52');
- the minutes of rows 46-49 are read as 56'/57' (not 16'/17');
- the four reduced values 50.65, 52.30, 55.20, 56.20 are assigned to n = 46, 47, 48, 49 respectively.

The drift in r_n shows that the true period differs slightly from 30.60 s. Gauss's marginal note 'aus den 10 ersten 30"7' is the mean period from the first ten passages: (t10 - t1)/9 = 276.6/9 = 30.73 s if t1 = 23.8, or 276.8/9 = 30.76 s if t1 = 23.6. The first value rounds to 30.7. Over the whole run, (t49 - t1)/48 = 1471.8/48 = 30.66 s, taking t1 = 23.8.

(B) Period versus position. The data are:
- x = 156.65 mm: T = 20.10 s (previous page);
- x = 73.5 mm: T = 23.60 s;
- x = -4.7 mm: T = 30.60 s;
- another trial at x = 150.5 mm: T = 20.03 s.

Gauss notes that the CGs of rod and needle would coincide at x0 = 171.1 mm. This is presumably geometric: (L_rod - L_needle)/2.

Physics (my gloss): the system turns about the vertical through the combined CG. Hence I(x) = I_min + mu*(x - x0)^2, with mu = m_rod*m_needle/(m_rod + m_needle). Then T^2 = pi^2*I/(M*H) = a + b*(x - x0)^2, with its minimum where the centres of gravity coincide.

(C) Torsion. Two trials of 8 May show that re-hanging in the hook (a known rotation phi of the suspension) shifts the rest position by delta = 221.76 scale divisions. Gauss concludes: torsion = 1/108.76 of the total (magnetic) directive force. Then he writes 'statisches Moment der Torsion = 94.7'.

Implicit steps (mine):
- In equilibrium, M*H*sin(delta) = tau*(phi - delta), so theta = tau/(M*H) = delta/(phi - delta).
- 1/108.76 therefore implies phi = 109.76*221.76, about 24,340 divisions in scale measure.
- The 94.7 implies a total static moment of about 108.76*94.7, roughly 10,300 in his units; 107.76*94.7, about 10,205, if 'gesammt' excludes the torsion part.

A third trial gives 213.68 and a fourth 226.98. Their mean is (213.68 + 226.98)/2 = 220.33. The mean of all four experiments, counting the 8-May value 221.76 as two experiments, is (2*221.76 + 220.33*2)/4 = 221.045, written 221.04.
errors: Row 1: with t1 = 1h33m23.6s the reduced value should be 1h32m53.0s, not 53.20. Either the raw time is really 23.8 (which also makes the first interval 30.8 s, in line with the others, and gives 30.73 s for the 10-period mean, matching '30.7') or there is a 0.2 s slip.

The 'Distanz wo die Schwerpunkte zusammenfallen = 171.1' does not fit the timings well under T^2 = a + b(x - x0)^2. A three-point fit to (156.65, 20.10), (73.5, 23.60), (-4.7, 30.60) gives x0 of about 164.3. Using 150.5/20.03 instead gives about 167.5. Fixing x0 = 171.1 and fitting the last two points predicts T of about 19.8 s at 156.65 (observed 20.10). Also 150.5 mm gave a shorter period than 156.65 mm, contrary to the model. This fits the note on the previous page, 'Confusion in den Distanzen 1 und 2', so 171.1 is probably geometric rather than fitted.

The late intervals (t47 - t46 = 32.25 s, t48 - t47 = 33.5 s) are irregular. Possibly passages alternate in direction with an off-centre rest point, or there was a disturbance. This is not a computational error.
The torsion rotation phi and the units of 94.7 are not stated, so 1/108.76 and 94.7 cannot be fully checked from this page alone.

results.what: Reduction of oscillation passage times by subtracting n times a provisional period, to get reduced epochs and refine the period
results.modern_name: Method of coincidences / reduced epochs for period determination (linear ephemeris residuals)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical timing practice; used by Gauss in magnetometer work 1832

results.what: Dependence of oscillation period on the position of the needle on the carrier rod; minimum moment of inertia when the centres of gravity coincide
results.modern_name: Parallel-axis (Huygens-Steiner) theorem applied to a two-body suspended system
results.usually_credited_to: Huygens / Steiner; applied in Gauss's Intensitas (1832-33)

results.what: Torsion coefficient of the suspension as the ratio of torsional to magnetic directive force, from the deflection on turning the suspension
results.modern_name: Torsion correction theta = delta/(phi - delta) in absolute magnetometry

results.what: Averaging repeated torsion trials (221.04 scale divisions)

deep.surprise_reason: These are laboratory notes from Gauss's well-documented 1832 absolute magnetic intensity experiments: period timing, inertia variation and torsion correction. All of this is published in substance in the Intensitas. The only interest is the raw data and small slips.

checkable.asserts: Row 3 reduction t3 - 3*30.6 = 1h32m53.6s (difference 0, within float rounding)
With t1 = 23.6 the reduced epoch is 53.0, not 53.20 (0 here shows the slip)
Mean period from first ten passages is about 30.73 s ('30.7')
Mean of third and fourth trials = 220.33
Implied suspension rotation in scale divisions if theta = delta/(phi - delta) = 1/108.76 (about 24340)
Implied total static moment about 10300 if torsion moment = total/108.76
Three-point fit of T^2 = a + b(x - x0)^2 gives x0 of about 164.3, not 171.1

transcription_corrections: Reduced-column minutes should read 1h32' (not 1h52'); every reduction t_n - n*30.60 lands at 1h32m5x s.
Raw times for rows 46-48 must be 1h56'/1h57' (the transcribed '16', '17' are 56, 57), as the reductions show.
The reduced values 50.65, 52.30, 55.20, 56.20 belong to rows 46, 47, 48, 49 respectively; the transcription misaligns them.
Row 8 raw time is 58.75 (verified by reduction to 53.95); row 10 raw time is 1h38m0.40s (verified).
Row 1 raw time may be 23"8 rather than 23"6 (consistent with reduced 53.20 and with the '30.7' mean).
'ein vierter 226.98' with the underlined mean 220.33 of the third and fourth trials; 'Mittel aus 4 Experim. 221,04' is correct.
